# my-work.md — Active Work Map

> **Template note.** This file stops the AI Chief of Staff from treating every project, email, and meeting as equally important. Fill in what is true now. Update when something starts, ships, pauses, or stops mattering. Do not try to make this complete on day one — fill the parts that change tomorrow's brief first (sections 1, 2, 3, 5).
>
> The `onboarding` behaviour drafts sections 1 to 3 from what it can read. Sections 1 (strategic priority) and 5 are decisions, so it will ask you rather than guess.

---

## 1. The business

**What we do:** [One sentence on the business. Plain English.]

**Who we serve:** [Primary customer / segment. Who pays us.]

**How we make money:** [The actual revenue model. Subscription, project, retainer, transaction, etc.]

**Current scale:** [Whatever number matters most. ARR, headcount, units, customers — pick the one the leader thinks in.]

**Current strategic priority (this quarter):** [The one thing the business is trying to do right now. If everything is a priority, nothing is.]

## 4. Open strategic loops

Decisions, commitments, or projects that are still live and still need movement. Different from `commitments.md` — those are specific promises to specific people. These are larger threads.

- [Open loop 1, e.g. "Decide whether to add a second sales hire this quarter."]
- [Open loop 2]
- [Open loop 3]

When one resolves, archive it (move to `archive/strategic-loops.md` or delete).

---

## 5. What we are not doing right now

The most important section. Without it, the AI Chief of Staff drifts the leader back toward whatever is tempting and visible.

- [Thing that keeps surfacing but should not be priority. e.g. "Not chasing enterprise deals this quarter."]
- [Thing the team wants the leader involved in but does not need them.]
- [Old initiative that should not pull attention. e.g. "Not reopening the [PRODUCT] discussion until next quarter."]
- [Topic the leader keeps drifting into. e.g. "Not redesigning the website this month."]

When a brief surfaces something from this list, flag it as a low-priority drift.

- **[%]** [Type of work. e.g. "Team leadership and 1:1s"]
- **[%]** [Type of work. e.g. "Strategic projects"]
- **[%]** [Type of work. e.g. "Admin, ops, and review"]
- **[%]** [Type of work. e.g. "Thinking and learning"]

---

## 7. Decision tradeoffs

When the AI Chief of Staff has to choose between competing priorities in a brief, use these defaults:

1. **Revenue-protecting work** beats **new opportunity work**, unless the new opportunity has a deadline.
2. **External commitments** beat **internal optimization**, unless the internal item is on a deadline.
3. **Decisions only the leader can make** beat **work the leader could delegate**, every time.
4. **Strategic priority items** (section 2) beat **drift items** (section 5), every time.

Override these only when `tomorrow.md` says otherwise.
